plan.target: Spurious Illegal Instruction Exception on sfence.vma Instruction When Virtual Memory is Disabled (src/privileged/privdec.sv)
plan.rationale: In `src/privileged/privdec.sv` line 82, the decode logic for `sfencevmaM` is erroneously gated with `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &`: `assign sfencevmaM = PrivilegedM & P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED & ((PrivilegeModeW == P.M_MODE & (vmaM | fenceinvalM)) | (PrivilegeModeW == P.S_MODE & (vmaM & ~STATUS_TVM | fenceinvalM)));`. In `privdec.sv` line 118, `IllegalPrivilegedInstrM` evaluates `PrivilegedM & ~(sretM|mretM|ecallM|ebreakM|wfiM|sfencevmaM)`. Under configurations where Supervisor mode is supported (`P.S_SUPPORTED == 1`) but virtual memory is disabled or unsupported (`P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`, such as `nodcache_rv64gc`), `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED` is 0, which forces `sfencevmaM` to 0. Consequently, `IllegalPrivilegedInstrM` evaluates to 1 and asserts `IllegalInstrFaultM = 1` at line 119. This causes Wally to erroneously raise an Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2) on any execution of `sfence.vma` in M-mode or in S-mode (with `TVM=0`). According to the RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume II: Privileged Architecture (Version 20211203), Section 4.2.1 ('Supervisor Memory-Management Fence Instruction (SFENCE.VMA)'), `SFENCE.VMA` is valid whenever S-mode is implemented (`P.S_SUPPORTED == 1`). The specification explicitly mandates: 'When address translation is not supported (i.e., satp.MODE is read-only 0 / Bare), SFENCE.VMA executes as a no-op (or flushes any implementation microarchitectural buffers) and does not raise an exception.' Furthermore, executing `SFENCE.VMA` in M-mode or S-mode (when `mstatus.TVM=0`) is strictly legal and must not trap. Testing under `nodcache_rv64gc` confirms that Spike executes `sfence.vma` legally and completes without exception (exit code 0), whereas unmodified Wally traps to Cause 2, causing an unhandled trap and triggering the testbench watchdog assertion failure (exit code 134).

   - In `nodcache_rv64gc`, executing `sfence.vma x0, x0` in M-mode or S-mode (with `mstatus.TVM=0`) evaluates `sfencevmaM = 0` due to `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0`, asserting `IllegalPrivilegedInstrM` and triggering an unhandled trap (Cause 2) on Wally. Architectural specification Section 4.2.1 mandates that `sfence.vma` must execute legally as a no-op when translation is not supported.

4. Test Strategy & Directed Testcases:
   - Create a deterministic assembly test suite `test_sfence_bare.S` in `$TEST_DIR/tests/` and link using a clean linker script (placing `.text` and `.data` starting at `0x80000000`, with `tohost` in `.data`):

     - Test 2 (Primary S-mode test): Configure PMP (`pmpaddr0 = -1`, `pmpcfg0 = 0x1f`) to allow full S/U memory access. Ensure `mstatus.TVM = 0`. Drop to S-mode via `mret` and execute `sfence.vma x0, x0`. Wally must not trap.
     - Test 3 (Negative control - TVM in S-mode): Set `mstatus.TVM = 1`, drop to S-mode, and execute `sfence.vma x0, x0`. Both Spike and Wally MUST trap to S-mode with Cause 2 (`scause == 2`). Catch the trap and return to M-mode.
     - Test 4 (Negative control - U-mode): Drop to U-mode and execute `sfence.vma x0, x0`. Both Spike and Wally MUST trap with Cause 2. Catch the trap and return to M-mode.
     - Success handler: Write 1 to 64-bit `tohost` followed by `1: j 1b` (`32'h6f`).
     - Failure handler: On an unexpected trap or if `mcause == 2` on Test 1 or 2, force unhandled watchdog abort (`csrw mtvec, x0; jr x0`) to terminate Verilator with exit code 134.

     - Run Wally (`./sim/verilator/wkdir/nodcache_rv64gc_testbench/Vtestbench +ElfFile=...`).
     - Exit 0 if Wally exits 0 (DUT correct).
     - Exit 1 if Wally exits 134 while Spike exits 0 (functional mismatch reproduced).

   - RISC-V Instruction Set Manual, Volume II: Privileged Architecture, Version 20211203:
     - Section 4.2.1 ('Supervisor Memory-Management Fence Instruction (SFENCE.VMA)'): 'The SFENCE.VMA instruction is valid only when S-mode is implemented. tester.report: A functional bug was successfully reproduced in Wally's Privileged Architecture decode logic. When virtual memory is disabled or unsupported (e.g. `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED == 0` under the `nodcache_rv64gc` configuration), executing the `sfence.vma` instruction raises a spurious Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2). In `src/privileged/privdec.sv` line 82, the execution of `sfence.vma` is improperly gated with `P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &`, which evaluates to 0 and asserts `IllegalPrivilegedInstrM`. fixer.report:
Root Cause: In src/privileged/privdec.sv line 82, sfencevmaM was gated with P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED instead of P.S_SUPPORTED. When Supervisor mode is supported (P.S_SUPPORTED=1) but virtual memory is disabled (P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED=0, e.g. nodcache_rv64gc), sfencevmaM was forced to 0, causing IllegalPrivilegedInstrM to assert and raising a spurious Illegal Instruction exception (Cause 2) on sfence.vma execution in M-mode or S-mode.

Minimal Fix: Single token change on line 82 of src/privileged/privdec.sv:
  BEFORE: assign sfencevmaM = PrivilegedM & P.VIRTMEM_SUPPORTED &
  AFTER:  assign sfencevmaM = PrivilegedM & P.S_SUPPORTED &

Specification: RISC-V Privileged Architecture v20211203 Section 4.2.1 mandates sfence.vma is valid whenever S-mode is implemented; when address translation is unsupported (Bare mode), it executes as a no-op without trapping.

Verification: Reproducer rebuilt and run against fixed DUT. Spike exit code 0 (correct). Wally DUT exit code 0 (previously 134 due to Cause 2 trap). Fix verified on nodcache_rv64gc configuration.

Files Changed: src/privileged/privdec.sv (line 82, 1 token changed). Backup of original at test_dir/fixer/privdec.sv.orig.
